title: A learned six-gene score associates with archived glioma survival
summary: Random-forest and LASSO selection produced a six-gene score associated with overall survival in archived lower-grade glioma data. The source also reports survival separation in three additional datasets using each cohort’s own median cutoff. This does not establish a fixed clinical threshold, a causal tumor mechanism or benefit from a selected drug.

source_review.scope: Primary data/model-construction Methods and survival Results only; no operational laboratory procedures reviewed

evidence.ai_role: Random forest and LASSO selected overlapping genes, followed by multivariable Cox scoring; the learned selection enables the represented expression-to-survival association.
evidence.tested: The source divided 497 TCGA cases into 348 development and 149 internal-validation records. Six genes remained after intersecting selectors and Cox refinement; survival comparisons were repeated in CGGA325, CGGA693 and GSE16011.
evidence.unknown: Prognostic screening before the split and reuse of the full TCGA cohort as Test2 limit independence. The three additional datasets used cohort-specific medians, so fixed-threshold validation is unestablished. Dataset overlap, endpoint harmonization and full preprocessing isolation were not independently reconstructed. Outcome-selected clusters are not newly verified biological subtypes; inferred immune activity and drug sensitivity are outside this result.
